chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The oath is returned to the claimant.

key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: The claimant, the party initiating the legal suit
key_terms.الْيَمِينُ: The oath, a legal instrument used to settle disputes

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on returning the oath to the claimant in Islamic courts?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith articulates the principle of *al-yamin* (oath) as a decisive evidentiary tool when the claimant (*mudda'i*) lacks sufficient proof (*bayyinah*) against a denying defendant. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that the oath is returned to the party who is better positioned to verify the truth, thereby resolving uncertainty in civil litigation through a solemn religious commitment.
